status: reviewer-motivated follow-up experiment (fair-comparison plan, 2026-09-09); NOT part of the original pre-specified experiment, and not part of the already-reported Task 20 naturalistic benchmark either -- see this script's module docstring
frozen_before_run_note: this file must be committed to git BEFORE any model request is issued -- the run step refuses to start unless it is tracked, has no uncommitted diff against HEAD, and its declaration hashes to fair_manifest_digest below

episode_source.reuse_note: the SAME 200 episodes as Task 20, reused verbatim (identical corrupted_string, true_action, and recalibrated confidence per episode) and referenced rather than copied, so there is exactly one source of truth for them. This experiment is a new set of ARMS over a frozen episode set, never a new draw
episode_source.confidence_used: the RECALIBRATED episode-level out-of-fold isotonic score from Task 19 (episode_confidence_per_episode.csv, column 'isotonic_episode') is used by BOTH the model's prompt (advisory arms) and the deterministic gate; the product score is kept only as confidence_product, for traceability, and is never rendered or gated on here

threshold_grid.note: matches nag.naturalistic.resolver_gate_curve's own default, so the hybrid arm and both resolver arms are swept over an identical grid and their AURCs are comparable without interpolation

fair:llm_vocab:advisory.reported_as: FIXED POINT -- an advisory arm's own decision is its final outcome, never swept
fair:llm_vocab:advisory.why: the information-symmetric counterpart of Task 20's factorial:decoder_confidence:advisory:s0 cell: identical harness, identical recalibrated confidence, the nine-command vocabulary added to the prompt

fair:llm_vocab:enforced.system_prompt: nag.naturalistic.build_naturalistic_system(cell, confidence) -- vocabulary disclosed; build_system withholds the numeric confidence for an enforced cell
fair:llm_vocab:enforced.reported_as: PROPOSAL -- run once, swept over threshold_grid downstream (covered & confidence >= t)
fair:llm_vocab:enforced.why: the information-symmetric counterpart of Task 20's factorial:decoder_confidence:enforced:s0 cell; one run serves every threshold because the model never sees one (nag.agent.run_episode_for_cell, same argument)

fair:hybrid_semantic_gate.harness: nag.naturalistic.run_hybrid_semantic_episode -- ONE call, no tools, no loop
fair:hybrid_semantic_gate.system_prompt: "" (empty) -- the whole prompt is build_hybrid_user, which already carries SINGLESHOT_SCAFFOLD and the nine-command vocabulary; mirrors nag.agent._run_singleshot, which likewise sends no system message
fair:hybrid_semantic_gate.reported_as: PROPOSAL -- called once at threshold=-inf, swept over threshold_grid downstream
fair:hybrid_semantic_gate.why: the reviewer's own proposed architecture: semantic correction from the model, admission from a deterministic threshold outside it. Confidence is deliberately withheld from this arm's prompt -- an architecture defined by keeping decoder uncertainty outside the model must not leak it back in through the prompt

fair:exact_resolver_gate.cost: zero API calls by construction; computed ONCE, not per model
fair:exact_resolver_gate.why: the swept version of Task 20's frozen natural_confidence_gate_canonical fixed point; exact match only, never repairs (canonical_action's own docstring)

fair:lexical_resolver_gate.cost: zero API calls by construction; computed ONCE, not per model
fair:lexical_resolver_gate.why: the PRIMARY COMPARATOR, now swept: the system the language models have to beat, and the one that motivated the information-symmetry fix (it is handed NATURAL_COMMANDS as a literal, so the models must be too)

proposal_threshold: -inf: the enforced and hybrid arms are called once per (model, episode) at a threshold that admits every parseable proposal, because the model never sees a threshold and cannot condition on one. Their rows record the PROPOSAL; coverage at threshold t is (covered & confidence >= t), swept downstream over threshold_grid
analysis_endpoints: the vocabulary-disclosed LLM arms against the SWEPT lexical resolver+gate curve, under symmetric information -- the comparison Task 20 could not make
the hybrid semantic-correction + deterministic-admission architecture against both the pure-LLM arms and the pure-resolver arms, on one risk-coverage frontier
whether the study's headline (no LLM arm beats a deterministic gate at matched coverage) survives once the models hold the same vocabulary the resolver does
reporting_note: absolute rates here are BENCHMARK ABSOLUTE RISKS AT THE SOURCE POOL'S OBSERVED decoder-error prevalence, never deployment estimates -- inherited unchanged from Task 20, whose episodes these are
